docs.title: Model results in directories
docs.text:
How a DirectoryArchive stores the simulations: the layout of the directories, the job name, the status, the persistent files, and a cache rebuilt from the archive.

from __future__ import annotations

import shutil
from pathlib import Path

from numpy import atleast_1d
from pandas import DataFrame

from vimseo import EXAMPLE_RUNS_DIR
from vimseo.api import create_model
from vimseo.api import load_model_results
from vimseo.api import search_model_results
from vimseo.core.model_settings import IntegratedModelSettings
from vimseo.storage_management.base_storage_manager import PersistencyPolicy

docs.title: Scratch, archive and cache
docs.text:
Three places hold the data of a simulation:

  • the scratch: the files of an external solver, disposable,
  • the archive: the inputs, the outputs and the metadata to keep, and the files the model declares persistent, copied from the scratch,
  • the cache: an HDF5 file avoiding to run a simulation twice; it can be rebuilt from the archive. A simulation served by the cache is not archived again.
archive = {
    "archive_manager": "DirectoryArchive",
    "directory_archive_root": EXAMPLE_RUNS_DIR
    / "archive/data_management/model_directory",
    "study_name": "my_study",
}
shutil.rmtree(archive["directory_archive_root"], ignore_errors=True)

model = create_model(
    "MockModelPersistent",
    "LC1",
    IntegratedModelSettings(
        **archive,
        directory_scratch_root=EXAMPLE_RUNS_DIR / "scratch/data_management",
        directory_scratch_persistency=PersistencyPolicy.DELETE_NEVER,
    ),
)
model.cache = None
model.execute({"x1": atleast_1d(2.0), "x2": atleast_1d(-2.0)})
model.execute({"x1": atleast_1d(3.0), "x2": atleast_1d(-1.0)})

Out:

{'x1': array([3.]), 'x2': array([-1.]), 'x3': array([1., 2., 3.]), 'y1': np.float64(2.0), 'y2': array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]), 'y3': array(['mock_string'], dtype='<U11'), 'y4': array([6.]), 'y5': array([  6.,  36., 216.]), 'error_code': array([0]), 'model': array(['MockModelPersistent'], dtype='<U19'), 'load_case': array(['LC1'], dtype='<U3'), 'description': array([''], dtype='<U1'), 'job_name': array([''], dtype='<U1'), 'persistent_result_files': array(['green_ellipse.png', 'blue_line.png'], dtype='<U17'), 'n_cpus': array([1]), 'date': array(['2026-10-28 09:53:23.732600'], dtype='<U26'), 'cpu_time': array([0.]), 'user': array(['sebastien.bocquet'], dtype='<U17'), 'machine': array(['PCBM20250036'], dtype='<U12'), 'vims_git_version': array(['4ebb9ae49db515984a3cb6e77a2dc2b5be975b05'], dtype='<U40'), 'directory_archive_root': array(['C:\\Users\\sebastien.bocquet\\Dev\\vddev\\docs\\runnable_examples\\model_runs\\archive\\data_management\\model_directory'],
      dtype='<U110'), 'directory_archive_job': array(['C:\\Users\\sebastien.bocquet\\Dev\\vddev\\docs\\runnable_examples\\model_runs\\archive\\data_management\\model_directory\\my_study\\MockModelPersistent\\LC1\\20261028T085323_9fde32c7'],
      dtype='<U168'), 'directory_scratch_root': array(['C:\\Users\\sebastien.bocquet\\Dev\\vddev\\docs\\runnable_examples\\model_runs\\scratch\\data_management'],
      dtype='<U94'), 'directory_scratch_job': array(['C:\\Users\\sebastien.bocquet\\Dev\\vddev\\docs\\runnable_examples\\model_runs\\scratch\\data_management\\MockModelPersistent\\LC1\\2'],
      dtype='<U120'), 'run_id': array(['20261028T085323_9fde32c7'], dtype='<U24'), 'tool_run_id': array([''], dtype='<U1'), 'study_name': array(['my_study'], dtype='<U8'), 'status': array(['FINISHED'], dtype='<U8')}

docs.title: The layout of the archive
docs.text:
A simulation is a directory {root}/{study}/{model}/{load_case}/{job}, named by its run_id: a path gives the identifier, an identifier gives the path. The run_id starts with the UTC date of the simulation, so that sorting the directories sorts the simulations chronologically.

Setting Path of a simulation Second execution default {root}/default_study/{model}/{load_case}/{run_id} a new directory, named by the new run_id study_name="my_study" {root}/my_study/{model}/{load_case}/{run_id} {root}/my_study/{model}/{load_case}/{other_run_id} job_name="my_job" {root}/default_study/{model}/{load_case}/my_job the same directory: fails, unless overwriting is accepted

The study of a model is changed between two executions with model.archive_manager.set_study_name("other_study").

archived_model_runs = search_model_results(**archive)
job_directory = Path(archived_model_runs[0]["uri"])
job_directory.relative_to(archive["directory_archive_root"])

Out:

WindowsPath('my_study/MockModelPersistent/LC1/20261028T085323_5f57cb9c')

sorted(path.name for path in job_directory.iterdir())

Out:

['blue_line.png', 'green_ellipse.png', 'results.json']

The JSON file holds the inputs, the outputs and the metadata, among which the status of the simulation: RUNNING from its start, then FINISHED or FAILED. The other files are the persistent files of the model.

docs.title: Find and load
docs.text:
The summaries come from the metadata of the JSON files; the uri is the job directory:

DataFrame(archived_model_runs)[["run_id", "study_name", "model_name", "status", "uri"]]
run_id study_name model_name status uri 0 20261028T085323_5f57cb9c my_study MockModelPersistent FINISHED C:\Users\sebastien.bocquet\Dev\vddev\docs\runn... 1 20261028T085323_9fde32c7 my_study MockModelPersistent FINISHED C:\Users\sebastien.bocquet\Dev\vddev\docs\runn...

The job directory is a reference of its model result, as is its run_id:

model_result = load_model_results(job_directory, **archive)[0]
model_result = load_model_results(archived_model_runs[0]["run_id"], **archive)[0]
(model_result.run_id, model_result.status, model_result.scalars(group="outputs"))

('20261028T085323_5f57cb9c', 'FINISHED', {'y1': np.float64(0.0), 'y4': np.float64(6.0)})

print(cache_from_archive)

docs.title: Model results in MLflow
docs.text:
How an MlflowArchive stores the simulations: one experiment per study, the mapping of the data to the metrics, params and tags of MLflow, and the queries.

This example needs the mlflow extra.

from __future__ import annotations

import shutil

from numpy import atleast_1d
from pandas import DataFrame

from vimseo import EXAMPLE_RUNS_DIR
from vimseo.api import create_model
from vimseo.api import load_model_results
from vimseo.api import search_model_results
from vimseo.utilities.optional_dependencies import import_optional

mlflow_tracking = import_optional("mlflow.tracking", "mlflow")

docs.title: The archive
docs.text:
The code is the one of the previous example, with archive_manager="MlflowArchive". directory_archive_root is the directory of a local MLflow database; a remote server is set in the configuration (VIMSEO_DATABASE__MODE=Team), and then directory_archive_root is ignored.

archive = {
    "archive_manager": "MlflowArchive",
    "directory_archive_root": EXAMPLE_RUNS_DIR / "archive/data_management/model_mlflow",
    "study_name": "my_study",
}
shutil.rmtree(archive["directory_archive_root"], ignore_errors=True)

model = create_model("BendingTestAnalytical", "Cantilever", **archive)
model.cache = None
for height in [40.0, 50.0, 60.0]:
    model.execute({"height": atleast_1d(height)})

docs.title: How a simulation is stored in MLflow
docs.text:
A study is one MLflow experiment, holding the simulations of all its models and its tool runs. A simulation is an MLflow run, named by its run_id, with:

  • metrics: the numbers among the inputs and the outputs (inputs.height, reaction_forces),
  • params: the other inputs and outputs, as JSON,
  • tags: the metadata, and vimseo.kind=simulation, vimseo.model, vimseo.load_case, vimseo.run_id to tell the runs of a study apart.

The run is created when the simulation starts, with the status RUNNING.

docs.title: Find and load
docs.text:
The VIMSEO functions are the same as for a DirectoryArchive; the uri is runs:/{mlflow_run_id}:

archived_model_runs = search_model_results(**archive)
DataFrame(archived_model_runs)[["run_id", "study_name", "inputs.height", "uri"]]
run_id study_name inputs.height uri 0 20261028T085318_60eb9ab5 my_study 50.0 runs:/873ec8cd4e3e4ff5a164ca2cd9048ba8 1 20261028T085318_f7ca45c1 my_study 40.0 runs:/7dd304967f71400f8308b34031dc0605 2 20261028T085319_1c5fe2b2 my_study 60.0 runs:/4d49757b4cbc4eb7baf0629517fe4a52

A query is the same for both archives, with or too, which the filters of MLflow do not support: the part joined by and is evaluated by the MLflow server, the rest by VIMSEO:

DataFrame(
    search_model_results(
        **archive,
        query="`inputs.height` > 45 and (`inputs.height` < 55 or status == 'FAILED')",
    )
)[["run_id", "inputs.height"]]
run_id inputs.height 0 20261028T085318_60eb9ab5 50.0

runs:/ also names the tool runs: loading the run of a tool run with load_model_results raises an error naming load_tool_results.

model_result = load_model_results(archived_model_runs[0]["uri"], **archive)[0]
figures = model_result.plot()

docs.title: Queries of MLflow
docs.text:
The MLflow client of the archive filters on any metric, param or tag; the same filter works in the user interface:

client = mlflow_tracking.MlflowClient(tracking_uri=model.archive_manager.uri)
experiment = client.get_experiment_by_name("my_study")
runs = client.search_runs(
    [experiment.experiment_id],
    filter_string="tags.`vimseo.kind` = 'simulation' and metrics.`inputs.height` > 45",
)
sorted(run.data.tags["vimseo.run_id"] for run in runs)

Out:

['20261028T085318_60eb9ab5', '20261028T085319_1c5fe2b2']

docs.title: A cache rebuilt from the archive
docs.text:
As with directories, only the finished simulations of the current study, model and load case are used:

print(model.create_cache_from_archive())

Out:

Name: node
   Type: HDF5Cache
   Tolerance: 1e-10
   Input names: ['height', 'imposed_dplt', 'length', 'nu_p', 'relative_dplt_location', 'width', 'young_modulus']
   Output names: ['cpu_time', 'date', 'description', 'directory_archive_job', 'directory_archive_root', 'directory_scratch_job', 'directory_scratch_root', 'dplt', 'dplt_at_force_location', 'dplt_grid', 'error_code', 'job_name', 'load_case', 'location_max_dplt', 'machine', 'maximum_dplt', 'model', 'moment', 'moment_grid', 'n_cpus', 'persistent_result_files', 'reaction_forces', 'run_id', 'status', 'study_name', 'tool_run_id', 'user', 'vims_git_version']

from __future__ import annotations

import shutil

from pandas import DataFrame

from vimseo import EXAMPLE_RUNS_DIR
from vimseo.api import create_model
from vimseo.api import load_model_results
from vimseo.api import load_tool_results
from vimseo.api import open_tool_archive
from vimseo.api import search_tool_runs
from vimseo.io.space_io import SpaceToolFileIO

from vimseo.tools.design_value.design_value_tool import DesignValueTool

docs.title: The tool runs
docs.text:
A design value executes two subtools: a DOE, which runs the simulations, and a statistical analysis. The subtools inherit the archive settings of their parent. The samples of the DOE are then replayed: the simulations come from the cache of the model, and are shared by the two tool runs.

archive = {
    "archive_manager": "DirectoryArchive",
    "directory_archive_root": EXAMPLE_RUNS_DIR
    / "archive/data_management/tool_directory",
    "study_name": "my_study",
}
shutil.rmtree(archive["directory_archive_root"], ignore_errors=True)

model = create_model(
    "BendingTestAnalytical",
    "ThreePoints",
    **archive,
    cache_file_path=archive["directory_archive_root"] / "cache.hdf",
)
parameter_space = (
    SpaceToolFileIO()
    .read(DESIGN_VALUE_LIB_DIR / "input_data" / "ElasticIsotropic_material_space.json")
    .parameter_space
)
design_value = DesignValueTool(**archive)
design_value.execute(
    inputs=DesignValueInputs(model=model, parameter_space=parameter_space),
    settings=DesignValueSettings(output_names=["reaction_forces"], n_samples=5),
)

docs.text:

        "tool_run_id": run["tool_run_id"],
        "parent": run["parent_tool_run_id"],
        "simulations": len(run.get("simulation_run_ids", [])),
        "key_values": run.get("key_values"),
    }
    for run in archived_tool_runs
])

def print_tree(parent_id: str = "", indent: str = "") -> None:
    for run in archived_tool_runs:
        if run["parent_tool_run_id"] == parent_id:
            print(f"{indent}- {run['tool_name']} {run['tool_run_id']}")
            print_tree(run["tool_run_id"], indent + "    ")

model.cache = None

docs.title: How a tool run is stored in MLflow
docs.text:
A tool run is an MLflow run of the experiment of its study, next to the simulations, with the tag vimseo.kind=tool_run. The run of a subtool is nested in the run of its parent. A tool run is described by:

  • tags vimseo.*: the tool_run_id, the tool, the study, the parent tool run, the class of the result, and the run_id of the simulations,
  • params: the settings of the tool,
  • metrics: the key values of the result, e.g. the mean of the reaction forces,
  • artifacts: the result in HDF5 format and its summary in JSON format,
  • the description, linking to the parent, the children and the simulations.

The searches are the same as with directories:

archived_tool_runs = search_tool_runs(**archive)
DataFrame(archived_tool_runs)[["tool_name", "tool_run_id", "uri", "key_values"]]
tool_name tool_run_id uri key_values 0 DOETool 20261028T085340_07066101 runs:/63b330fb267a4510b67e245e47531b09 {'n_samples': 5.0} 1 DesignValueTool 20261028T085340_ab69fc92 runs:/a3debacd0ca24deb802b637469646ca4 {'mean.reaction_forces': -37333.948114244115, ... 2 StatisticsTool 20261028T085342_5dcbb10a runs:/f1b27ba6146f4d7aa52d51993b8e9d38 {'mean.reaction_forces': -37333.948114244115, ...

By its tool_run_id or by its URI, here runs:/{mlflow_run_id}, the Run ID shown by the user interface of MLflow:

tool_run_id = design_value.result.metadata.tool_run_id
tool_result = load_tool_results(tool_run_id, **archive)[0]

uri = next(
    run["uri"] for run in archived_tool_runs if run["tool_run_id"] == tool_run_id
)
tool_result = load_tool_results(uri, **archive)[0]

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
A query of search_tool_runs reads the settings as inputs.{name} and the key values as outputs.{name}, e.g. the design values whose standard deviation of the reaction forces is lower than 100 N:

[
    run["tool_run_id"]
    for run in search_tool_runs(
        **archive,
        tool_name="DesignValueTool",
        query="`outputs.standard_deviation.reaction_forces` < 100",
    )
]

Out:

['20261028T085340_ab69fc92']

The MLflow client of the archive filters on the tags and the metrics too; the same filter works in the user interface:

tool_archive_manager = open_tool_archive(**archive)
client = mlflow_tracking.MlflowClient(tracking_uri=tool_archive_manager.uri)
experiment = client.get_experiment_by_name("my_study")
runs = client.search_runs(
    [experiment.experiment_id],
    filter_string="tags.`vimseo.kind` = 'tool_run' "
    "and tags.`vimseo.tool_name` = 'DesignValueTool' "
    "and metrics.`standard_deviation.reaction_forces` < 100",
)
[run.data.tags["vimseo.tool_run_id"] for run in runs]

Out:

['20261028T085340_ab69fc92']

The simulations used by a tool run, including the ones retrieved from the cache, carry its tool_run_id in their tag vimseo.tool_run_ids:

simulations = client.search_runs(
    [experiment.experiment_id],
    filter_string=f"tags.`vimseo.kind` = 'simulation' "
    f"and tags.`vimseo.tool_run_ids` LIKE '%{tool_run_id}%'",
)
len(simulations)

Out:

5

docs.text:
Filter the simulations of a study, find what varies between them, group them into families where a single input varies, and spot the duplicates.

from __future__ import annotations

import shutil

from numpy import atleast_1d

from vimseo import EXAMPLE_RUNS_DIR
from vimseo.api import create_model
from vimseo.api import open_model_results

docs.title: Open the results of a study
docs.text:
open_model_results reads the summaries of the archive and returns a ModelResults, an immutable collection. A result is loaded only when it is used:

model_results = open_model_results(**archive)
model_results

Out:

ModelResults(8 model results, study_name ['beam_study'], model_name ['BendingTestAnalytical'], status {'FINISHED': 8})

docs.title: Filter
docs.text:
filter keeps the results matching every condition and returns a new collection. failed=False drops the failed simulations (a status other than FINISHED, or a positive error_code). ignoring excludes a numerical setting from the comparisons; it stays in the results:

results_for_convergence = model_results.filter(
    model_name="BendingTestAnalytical", failed=False
).ignoring("imposed_dplt")
len(results_for_convergence)

Out:

8

docs.title: What varies
docs.text:
varying_inputs lists the inputs taking several values; imposed_dplt is left out, since the collection ignores it:

results_for_convergence.varying_inputs()
n_values values input width 3 [20.0, 25.0, 30.0] height 4 [30.0, 40.0, 50.0, 60.0]

docs.title: Families along one input
docs.text:
families(along=...) groups the results which differ by this input only. The key of a family is the value of the other varying inputs; the results alone in their group are reported:

families = results_for_convergence.families(along="height")
families

Out:

Families(along='height', ignoring=('imposed_dplt',), 2 families, 1 ungrouped)
  width=20.0   ModelResults(4, [30.0, 40.0, 40.0, 50.0])
  width=30.0   ModelResults(3, [30.0, 40.0, 50.0])
  ungrouped   ['20261028T085322_48d5133f']

A family is a collection, which superposes the curves of its results, labelled by the value of the varying input:

family = families.get(width=20.0)
family.visualize(plot_names=["moment_vs_moment_grid"])["moment_vs_moment_grid"]

The figures of all the families show their scalar outputs versus the varying input:

figures = families.visualize()
figures["scalar_outputs_vs_height[width=20.0]"]

docs.text:
Two simulations with the same inputs are reported, never deleted:

results_for_convergence.duplicates()[
    ["group", "run_id", "inputs.height", "inputs.width"]
]

docs.title: Explore a set of tool results
docs.text:
Filter the tool runs of a study, find which settings vary between them, group them into families where a single setting varies, and spot the duplicates.

from __future__ import annotations

import shutil

from vimseo import EXAMPLE_RUNS_DIR
from vimseo.api import create_model
from vimseo.api import open_tool_results
from vimseo.io.space_io import SpaceToolFileIO
from vimseo.tools.design_value import DESIGN_VALUE_LIB_DIR
from vimseo.tools.design_value.design_value_tool import DesignValueInputs
from vimseo.tools.design_value.design_value_tool import DesignValueSettings
from vimseo.tools.design_value.design_value_tool import DesignValueTool

docs.title: A study
docs.text:
A convergence study of the design value of the reaction force of a beam: two DOE algorithms and three numbers of samples, with a tool run done twice and one done with another coverage of the tolerance interval.

archive = {
    "archive_manager": "DirectoryArchive",
    "directory_archive_root": EXAMPLE_RUNS_DIR
    / "archive/data_management/explore_tools",
    "study_name": "design_value_study",
}
shutil.rmtree(archive["directory_archive_root"], ignore_errors=True)

model = create_model("BendingTestAnalytical", "ThreePoints", **archive)
model.cache = None
parameter_space = (
    SpaceToolFileIO()
    .read(DESIGN_VALUE_LIB_DIR / "input_data" / "ElasticIsotropic_material_space.json")
    .parameter_space
)


def compute_design_value(**settings) -> None:
    """Compute the design value of the reaction force with some settings."""
    DesignValueTool(**archive).execute(
        inputs=DesignValueInputs(model=model, parameter_space=parameter_space),
        settings=DesignValueSettings(output_names=["reaction_forces"], **settings),
    )


for algo in ("OT_MONTE_CARLO", "OT_LHS"):
    for n_samples in (5, 10, 20):
        compute_design_value(algo=algo, n_samples=n_samples)
compute_design_value(algo="OT_LHS", n_samples=10)
compute_design_value(algo="OT_LHS", n_samples=40, coverage=0.1)

docs.title: Open the tool results of a study
docs.text:
open_tool_results reads the summaries of the archive and returns a ToolResults, an immutable collection. A result is loaded only when it is used. The inputs of a tool run are its scalar settings and its outputs are its key values. The archive holds the design values and their subtools, the DOEs and the statistical analyses:

tool_results = open_tool_results(**archive)
tool_results

Out:

ToolResults(24 tool results, study_name ['design_value_study'], tool_name ['DOETool', 'DesignValueTool', 'StatisticsTool'], status {'FINISHED': 24})

docs.title: Filter
docs.text:
The results of different tools cannot be compared: filter keeps those of the design value tool. failed=False drops the failed tool runs. ignoring excludes a setting from the comparisons; it stays in the results:

design_values = tool_results.filter(tool_name="DesignValueTool", failed=False).ignoring(
    "coverage"
)
len(design_values)

Out:

8

docs.title: What varies
docs.text:
varying_inputs lists the settings taking several values; coverage is left out, since the collection ignores it:

design_values.varying_inputs()
n_values values input n_samples 4 [5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 40.0] algo 2 [OT_LHS, OT_MONTE_CARLO]

docs.title: Families along one setting
docs.text:
families(along=...) groups the tool runs which differ by this setting only. The key of a family is the value of the other varying settings. Since coverage is ignored, the tool run with 40 samples belongs to the family of OT_LHS:

families = design_values.families(along="n_samples")
families

Out:

Families(along='n_samples', ignoring=('coverage',), 2 families, 0 ungrouped)
  algo=OT_LHS   ToolResults(5, [5.0, 10.0, 10.0, 20.0, 40.0])
  algo=OT_MONTE_CARLO   ToolResults(3, [5.0, 10.0, 20.0])

The figures of the families show their key values versus the varying setting, here the mean and the standard deviation of the reaction force:

figures = families.visualize()
figures["scalar_outputs_vs_n_samples[algo=OT_LHS]"]

docs.title: Duplicates
docs.text:
Two tool runs with the same settings are reported, never deleted:

design_values.duplicates()[["group", "tool_run_id", "inputs.algo", "inputs.n_samples"]]
group tool_run_id inputs.algo inputs.n_samples 4 0 20261028T085334_4b02d441 OT_LHS 10.0 6 0 20261028T085337_9b1ecc39 OT_LHS 10.0

docs.title: How to configure VIMSEO with a .env file
docs.text:
VIMSEO's global configuration can be overridden with environment variables, or with a .env file placed in the directory from which VIMSEO is run. Every setting is exposed as an environment variable prefixed with VIMSEO_; nested settings are reached with a double underscore (__) as separator. Process environment variables take precedence over the .env file.

Here is a full example, covering every available setting:

VIMSEO_LOGGING="info"
VIMSEO_SOLVERS__DUMMY__JOB_EXECUTOR="InteractiveAbaqus"
VIMSEO_ROOT_DIRECTORY=""
VIMSEO_WORKING_DIRECTORY=""
VIMSEO_RUN_ARCHIVE_MANAGER="DirectoryArchive"
VIMSEO_DATABASE__MODE="Local"
VIMSEO_DATABASE__LOCAL_URI=""
VIMSEO_DATABASE__TEAM_URI="https://mlflow.irt-aese.local/"
VIMSEO_DATABASE__USERNAME=""
VIMSEO_DATABASE__PASSWORD=""
VIMSEO_DATABASE__USE_INSECURE_TLS=False
VIMSEO_DATABASE__SSL_CERTIFICATE_FILE=""
VIMSEO_STUDY_NAME="default_study"

Parameters:

Environment variable Description Default VIMSEO_LOGGING Logging verbosity (e.g. "info", "debug") "info" VIMSEO_SOLVERS__<name>__JOB_EXECUTOR The job executor used by the solver <name> (must be a registered job executor class, e.g. "InteractiveAbaqus") None VIMSEO_SOLVERS__<name>__COMMAND_RUN The command used by the solver <name> to run a job "" VIMSEO_SOLVERS__<name>__COMMAND_PRE The command used by the solver <name> for its pre-processing step "" VIMSEO_SOLVERS__<name>__COMMAND_POST The command used by the solver <name> for its post-processing step "" VIMSEO_ROOT_DIRECTORY The root directory where tool results are written "" VIMSEO_WORKING_DIRECTORY The working directory where tool results are written. If empty, results are exported to unique directories created under the root directory; if set, results are exported under this path "" VIMSEO_RUN_ARCHIVE_MANAGER The archive manager backend of the simulations (e.g. "DirectoryArchive", "MlflowArchive") "DirectoryArchive" VIMSEO_DATABASE__MODE The database mode, "Local" or "Team" "Local" VIMSEO_DATABASE__LOCAL_URI The URI of the local MLflow tracking server "" VIMSEO_DATABASE__TEAM_URI The URI of the team's shared MLflow tracking server "https://mlflow.irt-aese.local/" VIMSEO_DATABASE__USERNAME The username used to authenticate against the MLflow tracking server "" VIMSEO_DATABASE__PASSWORD The password used to authenticate against the MLflow tracking server "" VIMSEO_STUDY_NAME The study in which the simulations and the tool runs are archived "default_study" VIMSEO_DATABASE__USE_INSECURE_TLS Whether to skip TLS certificate verification False VIMSEO_DATABASE__SSL_CERTIFICATE_FILE Path to a custom SSL certificate file ""

Note: solvers is a mapping from solver name to its configuration, so <name> above can be any key you choose (e.g. dummy, abaqus). The default configuration already defines a dummy and an abaqus solver; setting VIMSEO_SOLVERS__<name>__... for a new name adds a new solver entry.

docs.title: How to write logs to a file with VIMSEO
docs.text:
To redirect VIMSEO logs to a file, call vimseo.api.activate_logger with a filename. A timestamped file name avoids overwriting previous runs.

import logging
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path
from vimseo.api import activate_logger

# Define your working directory
working_directory = Path("path/to/output")
working_directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Generate a unique timestamp down to the millisecond
now = datetime.now()
timestamp = now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S-") + f"{now.microsecond // 1000:03d}"

# Activate the logger
activate_logger(
    level=logging.INFO,
    filename=working_directory / f"log_{timestamp}.txt",
    filemode="w",
)

This will create a log file such as log_2026-06-11_14-32-45-123.txt in the specified directory.

Parameters:

Parameter Description Default level Logging verbosity as a logging level value. If not provided, the level from the VIMSEO configuration is used None filename Path to the log file. If empty, logs go to the console only "" filemode "w" to overwrite, "a" to append "a"

Note: By default (filename=""), logs are printed to the console only. Providing a filename adds a file handler; the console output is kept as well. When an Abaqus job runs, its convergence files (.sta, .msg) are surfaced through the same logger, so they end up in this file too. The .sta progress lines are prefixed with ▓▓ SOLVER[sta] ▓▓ so they pop out of the solver's stdout (and are easy to grep); the more verbose .msg lines carry a plain [solver msg] tag.

docs.title: Integration of models
docs.text:
Integrate the models of interest is the first mandatory step before using the VV&UQ methods of VIMSEO. As a result, VIMSEO should make model integration as easy as possible, and provide a range of examples to illustrate different ways of integrating models.

VIMSEO follows a component-based approach for model integration. A model contains a list of executable components, which are run sequentially. To learn more about the advantages of this approach, you can refer to model integration explanation

docs.title: Integration of a GEMSEO discipline
docs.text:
A GEMSEO discipline can be easily turned into a VIMSEO model, by deriving a class from BaseDisciplineModel and setting the _DISCIPLINE class attribute:

# Copyright 2021 IRT Saint Exupery, https://www.irt-saintexupery.com
#
# This program is free software; you can redistribute it and/or
# modify it under the terms of the GNU Lesser General Public
# License version 3 as published by the Free Software Foundation.
#
# This program is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
# but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
# MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.  See the GNU
# Lesser General Public License for more details.
#
# You should have received a copy of the GNU Lesser General Public License
# along with this program; if not, write to the Free Software Foundation,
# Inc., 51 Franklin Street, Fifth Floor, Boston, MA  02110-1301, USA.

"""A model in asymptotic convergence by construction.

Notations are taken from:
https://asmedigitalcollection.asme.org/verification/article/7/3/031005/1146443/Confidence-Intervals-for-Richardson-Extrapolation
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from gemseo.disciplines.analytic import AnalyticDiscipline
from numpy import atleast_1d

from vimseo.core.base_discipline_model import BaseDisciplineModel
from vimseo.core.model_metadata import MetaDataNames

ORDER = 2
mock_convergence_discipline = AnalyticDiscipline({
    "a_h": "a - a_n * h**n - a_m * h**m",
    "n_dof": "1. / h**3",
    MetaDataNames.cpu_time.name: "1.0",
})
mock_convergence_discipline.default_input_data = {
    "a": atleast_1d(1.0),
    "a_n": atleast_1d(0.1),
    "h": atleast_1d(2),
    "n": atleast_1d(ORDER),
    "a_m": atleast_1d(0.0),
    "m": atleast_1d(ORDER + 1),
}


class MockConvergence(BaseDisciplineModel):
    _DISCIPLINE = mock_convergence_discipline
    _EXPECTED_LOAD_CASE = "Dummy"

If you have a model implemented in a Python script, you may integrate the process to VIMSEO by:

  • wrapping this model in a GEMSEO discipline
  • using the above procedure to convert it as a VIMSEO model

docs.text:
If you have a model implemented in a Python script, and want to integrate it as a three-step pre-processing, run-processing and post-processing:

from __future__ import annotations

from vimseo.core.pre_run_post_model import PreRunPostModel


class MockModel(PreRunPostModel):
    """Mock Class to test the creation of a model."""

    SUMMARY = (
        " A toy model implementing an unphysical analytical law;"
        " used for testing purpose"
    )
    PRE_PROC_FAMILY = "MockPre"  # x2 = x1 + 2
    RUN_FAMILY = "MockRun"  # y0 = x2 * 2
    POST_PROC_FAMILY = "MockPost"  # y1 = y0 + 1

# Copyright 2021 IRT Saint Exupery, https://www.irt-saintexupery.com
#
# This program is free software; you can redistribute it and/or
# modify it under the terms of the GNU Lesser General Public
# License version 3 as published by the Free Software Foundation.
#

# but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
# MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.  See the GNU
# Lesser General Public License for more details.
#
# You should have received a copy of the GNU Lesser General Public License
# along with this program; if not, write to the Free Software Foundation,
# Inc., 51 Franklin Street, Fifth Floor, Boston, MA  02110-1301, USA.

from __future__ import annotations

from numpy import array
from numpy import atleast_1d

from vimseo.core.components.base_component import BaseComponent
from vimseo.problems.mock import X1_DEFAULT_VALUE


class MockPre(BaseComponent):
    """Mock Class for pre-processing."""

    USE_JOB_DIRECTORY = False


class MockPre_LC1(MockPre):
    """Mock Class for pre-processing with a load case."""

    def __init__(self, **options) -> None:
        super().__init__(**options)
        self.default_input_data.update({
            "x1": atleast_1d(X1_DEFAULT_VALUE),
            "x1_maximum_only": atleast_1d(X1_DEFAULT_VALUE),
            "x1_minimum_only": atleast_1d(X1_DEFAULT_VALUE),
            "x1_no_bounds": atleast_1d(X1_DEFAULT_VALUE),
        })

    def _run(self, input_data):
        x1 = input_data["x1"]
        x2 = x1 + 2
        return {"x2": x2}


class MockRun(BaseComponent):
    """Mock Class for run."""

    def _run(self, input_data):
        x2 = input_data["x2"]
        y0 = x2 * 2
        return {"y0": y0}


class MockPost(BaseComponent):
    """Mock Class for post-processing."""


class MockPost_LC1(MockPost):
    """Mock Class for post-processing with a loadcase."""

    def _run(self, input_data):
        y0 = input_data["y0"]
        y1 = y0 + 1
        return {"y1": y1, "error_code": array([0])}

class MockModelWithMaterial(MockModel):

    SUMMARY = "A toy model loading a material"

docs.title: Case of multiple layups
docs.text:
When running a study involving simulations of several layups, one current limitation is that VIMSEO cannot process the cache file if these layups have different lengths. The simulations are correctly stored in the cache but trying to convert the cache to a dataset or calling the executable cache_viewer (see handling_failed_simulations) to visualize the cache entries will fail.

To overcome this issue, one approach is to prefix the cache file name by the layup, which segregates the caches by layups. Thus, at model instanciation, specify the cache_file_path like this:

from vimseo.api import create_model
from vimseo.utilities.database import encode

model_name = "OpfmCube"
load_case = "PST"
model = create_model(
    model_name, load_case,
    cache_file_path=f"layup{encode(layup)}_{model_name}_{load_case}_cache.hdf"
)

In addition, since the layup strongly controls the physics of the laminate, it may be interesting to separate the tool results and the individual simulations per layup. Give the model and the tools the same study_name, one per layup: they are archived in the same archive, under {directory_archive_root}/{study_name}/ (or in the MLflow experiment {study_name}), and stay linked to each other.

from vimseo.api import create_model
from vimseo.utilities.database import encode

model_name = "OpfmCube"
load_case = "PST"
study_name = f"layup{encode(layup)}"
model = create_model(
    model_name, load_case,
    cache_file_path=f"{study_name}_{model_name}_{load_case}_cache.hdf",
    study_name=study_name,
)

And create the tool like this:

from vimseo.tools.sensitivity.sensitivity import SensitivityTool

tool = SensitivityTool(study_name=study_name)

The study of a whole script can also be set once, with the environment variable VIMSEO_STUDY_NAME.

docs.title: CALMIP
docs.text:
Note

The generic project a_project used as example in the documentation should be replaced by vimseo, and a_plugin by the considered VIMSEO plugin (e.g. vims_composites).

VIMSEO is first installed on CALMIP.

Note

The below procedure explains a user-mode installation, which means that VIMSEO sources are frozen in the environment. Modification of the sources do not modify the environment unless you re-install. For developers, you can also install VIMSEO in developer-mode

First load a Python environment (provided by conda on CALMIP), with a Python version compatible with VIMSEO:

module load python/3.11.3

The easiest way is to install with pip: Create an empty python environment and activate and install.

If you work in a VIMSEO plugin, you also need to install it.

Warning

For the moment, the subroutine compilation does not work on CALMIP. So you can skip the subroutine installation pip install src/extensions. It means that the UnitCell models will not work. Since they are fast, they can be easily run on another machine.

Note

Running module load python/3.11.3 is only necessary at the generation of VIMSEO environment. Then, a python is available in this environment, so activating it is sufficient to have python. Once the environment is installed, to run simulations, we recommend the following procedure:

  • deactivate the conda base env which is automatically activated: conda deactivate
  • do not run module load python/3.11.3 to avoid conflicts with VIMSEO environment
  • activate VIMSEO environment

Then, load the Abaqus module, necessary to execute Abaqus CAE in interactive mode (used in the model pre and post processors):

module load abaqus/2022

Note that by default, Abaqus points to licence server 27000@ica-abaqus.insa-toulouse.fr. To use IRT licence server, you can copy-paste the below instruction in a file abaqus_v6.env placed in your home:

license_server_type=FLEXNET
abaquslm_license_file="27001@license-abaqus.pf.irt-saintexupery.com"
academic=RESEARCH

On CALMIP, it is recommended to store job outputs on /tmpdir, so you may work in this directory, typically /tmpdir/${USER}/my_wkdir.

On a HPC cluster, you need to submit jobs through a job scheduler. So, the run-processor of the wrapper must use a job executor which will execute Abaqus through the job scheduler of the cluster. To do so, you can override the configuration by placing a config file in your working directory. Copy the below instruction in a file whose name ends with .config in your working directory:

{
"N_CPUS": "",
"JOB_EXECUTOR": "SlurmAbaqus",
"CMD_ABAQUS_CAE": "abq2022hf1 cae noGUI={{abaqus_script}}",
"CMD_ABAQUS_RUN": "",
"LOGGER_MODE": "info",
"TEST_LOGGER_MODE": "info",
"ROOT_DIRECTORY": "",
"WORKING_DIRECTORY": "",
"VIMS_TEST_DIR": "/tmp/tests",
"CMD_ABAQUS_CAE_POST": ""
}

The pre and post processors always use an interactive job executor. The command executed by these two processors are the above CMD_ABAQUS_CAE. For a job executor of type BaseJobScheduler, as it is the case for the SlurmAbaqus job executor, the Abaqus command executed through the job scheduler is defined by the class attribute _COMMAND_TEMPLATE of the job executor class. It is tested for Abaqus jobs submitted through the Slurm job scheduler available on CALMIP, and in principle should not be modified. You can still override this default command by specifying a non-empty command in the configuration variable CMD_ABAQUS_RUN.

You can test that VIMSEO can submit a job by executing the below script (to be copy-pasted in a .py file):

from vimseo.api import create_model
from vimseo.api import create_model, activate_logger, LOGGER_LEVELS

activate_logger(level=LOGGER_LEVELS["info"])

model = create_model("OpfmPlate", "PST", check_subprocess=True, directory_naming_method="NUMBERED")
model.cache = None
model.set_n_cpus(12)
print(model._run_processor.n_cpus)
model.execute()
print(model.get_output_data())

Another key point is to avoid that your VIMSEO Python process being killed when your connexion to the cluster closes. There are two possibilities:

  • run you Python command in nohup: 

    nohup python my_vims_script.py 2>&1 | tee out.txt &

  • use tmux, a terminal emulator. A command launched in tmux will persist after the connexion closes:

tmux
python my_vims_script.py 2>&1 | tee out.txt

To reattach to the tmux session, first list the available sessions with tmux ls, and attach to the desired session with tmux attach-session -t i where i is the i-th session.

docs.title: Handling failed simulation
docs.text:
VIMSEO Abaqus wrapper allows to be tolerant to some errors occurring during a model execution. The tolerance to error can be controlled with argument check_subprocess at model creation:

  • setting check_subprocess to True should normally raise a CalledSubprocessError error either if one of the subprocess of the pre, run and post processors fails, or if the outputs of the run-processor are not as expected by method ~.check_job_completion. If the model is running by a scenario, the scenario should also fail. The failed model simulation is not stored in the model cache. So after debugging, if the same scenario is run again, the model should be fully re-executed.

  • setting check_subprocess to False (default behaviour) makes the model more tolerant to errors. If one of the subprocess of the pre, run and post processors fails, or if the outputs of the run-processor are not as expected, NaN values are set to model outputs, the error code in the model output is set to one, and the model execution terminates without error. As a result, this simulation is stored in the cache. This may cause a problem when, after debugging, the user wants to re-execute the model (or the scenario executing the model), because the cache will be activated and will return the NaN outputs previously obtained. To enable full re-execution of the model, the cache entry corresponding to these inputs must be deleted from the cache.

To help the user manage the cache (which can be seen here as a database of model executions), two executables are accessible from a terminal where the environment in which VIMSEO is installed is activated:

  • cache_viewer. You may enter cache_viewer -h to get some help. It allows to visualize the cache content as a dataset, with some options to filter some entries.

  • cache_delete_entry. You may enter cache_delete_entry -h to get some help. It allows to delete an entry, typically one having an error code to one and that you want to fully re-execute.

Warning

At the moment, there is an assumption that the cache entry index and the index of the dataset row shown with cache_viewer are the same. This may be wrong if you remove another entry than the last ones. The problem is that you may try to delete non-existing entries when you will view the cache again, after having deleted entries. If cache_delete_entry bugs, you can also use the hdfview tool, which is a standard tool for hdf5 file manipulation. hdfview allows to delete hdf groups and thus can be used in replacement of cache_delete_entry.

docs.title: Run Abaqus models using a Docker container
docs.text:
A Docker container where Abaqus is installed is available. In a terminal, run:

docker login https://registry-elliot-fire.pf.irt-saintexupery.com/

with :

user: firetracker
password: 31onFire34

Then, pull the images:

docker pull registry-elliot-fire.pf.irt-saintexupery.com/abaqus:2022-int
docker pull registry-elliot-fire.pf.irt-saintexupery.com/abaqus:2022-ext

Warning

The image is heavy, make sure you have at least 25 Go available on your disk.

The 2022-int tag is configured to use the internal URL to licence server, and the 2022-ext is configured to use the external URL to licence server.

docs.title: Run Abaqus model on Linux
docs.text:
Copy this code block in your .bashrc file:

export ABAQUS_DOCKER_IMAGE_NAME="registry-elliot-fire.pf.irt-saintexupery.com/abaqus:2022-int"
function abq_2022_docker() {
    local CURRENT_DIR
    CURRENT_DIR=$(pwd)
    docker run --rm -v "${CURRENT_DIR}":"${CURRENT_DIR}" --workdir "${CURRENT_DIR}" -it ${ABAQUS_DOCKER_IMAGE_NAME} abq2022 interactive $*
}

Then, source it:

source ~/.bashrc

You should now be able to call Abaqus in a shell by using the defined function (abq_2022_docker here, it can be renamed as you wish).

docs.title: Run Abaqus model on Windows
docs.text:
You need to install Docker Desktop, which can be found on IRT application portal (type Software center in the Windows search bar).

Note

Docker Desktop requires the Windows System Linux (WSL). To install it, issue a ticket to the IT. You must also add your user to the Docker group, which should also be done through a ticket to the IT.

In Docker Desktop, in the Images tab, search for the above image and run it. Make sure that the engine is running.

Then, copy the below code snippet in a .bat file (for example abq_2022_docker.bat):

@echo off
setlocal
set ABAQUS_DOCKER_IMAGE_NAME=registry-vimseo.pf.irt-saintexupery.com/abaqus:2022-int
set CURRENT_DIR=%cd%
docker run --rm -v "%CURRENT_DIR%":"/workdir" --workdir "/workdir" %ABAQUS_DOCKER_IMAGE_NAME% abq2022 %*
REM setx PATH "%PATH%;C:\Scripts"
REM setx PATHEXT %PATHEXT%;.
endlocal

docs.title: First interactive test
docs.text:
Before running VIMSEO Abaqus models, an interactive test in a terminal can be done (git CMD or Powershell):

  • Add the above .bat file to the PATH (in Windows menu, select Modify environment variable for your account and add the directory containing the .bat file to the PATH variable),

  • modify the .bat file to add the -it option to docker run: 

    docker run --rm -v "%CURRENT_DIR%":"/workdir" --workdir "/workdir" -it %ABAQUS_DOCKER_IMAGE_NAME% abq2022 %*

Then move to an existing VIMSEO job directory where an Abaqus was run, and run the Abaqus command line as specified by VIMSEO Abaqus wrapper. For instance, to run the pre-processing and run-processing for a model with subroutines:

abq_2022_docker cae noGUI={{abaqus_script}}
abq_2022_docker interactive job={{job_name}} cpus={{n_cpus}} user=index_subroutines.f

docs.title: VIMSEO model execution
docs.text:
To run a VIMSEO Abaqus model on Windows, use the following VIMSEO configuration:

"CMD_ABAQUS_CAE": "C:/Users/Public/docker_abaqus/abq_2022_docker.bat cae noGUI={{abaqus_script}}",
"CMD_ABAQUS_RUN": "C:/Users/Public/docker_abaqus/abq_2022_docker.bat job={{job_name}} cpus={{n_cpus}}{% if subroutine_names|length > 0 %} user={{subroutine_names[0]}}{% endif %} {% if is_implicit == False %}double=both {% endif %}inter",

(The path to the .bat is an example, but the idea is to use linux-like path (/)). Also, make sure that the -it option in the docker run command of the .bat file is removed.

docs.title: Set up a parameter space
docs.text:
A space of uncertain parameters is an input to several tools in VIMSEO: for instance a sensitivity analysis, a DOE, a model to model code verification. Setting up a parameter space with a large number of variables requires to specify a large number of options. In VIMSEO, the tool in charge of generating a parameter space is the so called SpaceTool. The variables are in general treated by groups. For example, the first group has a normal distribution centered on the model default value, and second group has a uniform distribution spanning the entire variable range. The SpaceTool allows to set up a parameter space by successive updates. At each update, a list of variables, a SpaceBuilder and its settings can be selected. Four SpaceBuilder are available: - FromModelCenterAndCov: suited to set up distributions based on model default values and a coefficient of variation. Note that the center of the distribution can be chosen based on a relationship between the minimum and maximum bounds of the variable, but it requires that both bounds are defined. - FromModelMinAndMax: suited to set up distributions from the bounds of the variables if both bounds are defined. - FromCenterAndCov - FromMinAndMax

The last two are agnostic of the model.

Even if this process can be performed programmatically, being able to visualize the chosen distributions and how they are located with respect to the model bounds is very useful. Indeed, the distributions can be truncated by the bounds and, for example, a triangular distribution may have a shape very different from the expected one.

As a result, VIMSEO has a dedicated dashboard to set up a parameter space. The dashboard can be displayed by typing dashboard_space in a console where VIMSEO is installed. The following inputs can be used to initialize the parameter space: - a model - a SpaceTool result - a material values JSON file

If the model is the input, the parameter space can be initialized to the model material by ticking the checkbox From model material. Only the variables for which probability distributions are defined will be considered to build the parameter space.

For VIMSEO beam models, the default material defines probability distributions for the

As explained above, the parameter space can then be updated by first selecting in the sidebar the variables to modify:

Then the SpaceBuilder must be chosen, and its settings:

Then the Submit space parameters must be clicked.

The process of selecting variables, a space builer and its settings and validating by clicking the Submit space parameters can be repeated until the user is satisfied with the parameter space.

Note

To avoid setting distributions whose support is outside the model bounds, the model bounds can be shown by ticking the Show model bounds checkbox at the bottom of the sidebar. The part of the distribution which is outside the bounds is shown by a vertical red band.

The parameter space can finally be downloaded as a JSON file.

def activate_logger(
    level: int | None = None,
    filename: str | Path = "",
    filemode: str = "a",
):
    """Configure the VIMSEO (root) logger.

    Args:
        level: The logging level. If not provided, the level from the VIMSEO
            configuration is used.
        filename: The path to a log file. If provided, log records are also written
            to this file, in addition to the console.
        filemode: The file opening mode, either ``"a"`` (append) or ``"w"``
            (overwrite). Only used when ``filename`` is provided.
    """
    from gemseo import configure_logger

    if not level:
        from vimseo.config.global_configuration import _configuration as configuration

        level = _nameToLevel[configuration.logging.upper()]
    configure_logger(level=level, filename=filename, filemode=filemode)

def create_model(
    model_name: str,
    load_case_name: str = DUMMY_LOAD_CASE_NAME,
    model_options: IntegratedModelSettings | None = None,
    material: str | Path | Material | None = None,
    **options,
) -> IntegratedModel:
    """Create a model from its name.

    Args:
        model_name: string, name of the model to create
            (see :meth:`~vimseo.api.get_available_models` for valid names)
        load_case_name: The name of the load case that the model will execute.
        model_options: A pre-built :class:`.IntegratedModelSettings`. Any model option
            also passed as a keyword argument overrides the corresponding field.
        material: The material to build the model with, overriding the one its class
            declares in ``MATERIAL_FILE``. Either a material name
            (see :meth:`~vimseo.api.get_available_materials`), the path to a material
            JSON file, or a :class:`.Material`. By default, the model's own material
            is used.
        options: The options of the model.

    Returns: An instance of an :class:`.IntegratedModel`.
    """
    from vimseo.core.model_factory import ModelFactory

    if model_options is not None:
        options = {**model_options.model_dump(), **options}
    # Passed as a constructor keyword rather than through ``IntegratedModelSettings``:
    # that settings model is ``extra="forbid"`` and is round-tripped through
    # ``model_dump()``, which would flatten a ``Material`` instance into a plain dict.
    if material is not None:
        options["material"] = material
    return ModelFactory().create(model_name, load_case_name, **options)

get_available_load_cases(model_name: str) -> list[str]

Find the load cases available for this model.

Parameters:

  • model_name (str) –

    The model name.

Returns:

  • list[str] –

    The load cases associated with the specified model.

Source code in src\vimseo\api.py 
def get_available_load_cases(model_name: str) -> list[str]:
    """Find the load cases available for this model.

    Args:
        model_name: The model name.

    Returns:
        The load cases associated with the specified model.
    """
    from vimseo.core.load_case_factory import LoadCaseFactory
    from vimseo.core.model_factory import ModelFactory

    lc_factory = LoadCaseFactory()
    model_class = ModelFactory().get_class(model_name)
    domain = model_class._LOAD_CASE_DOMAIN
    all_load_case_names = []
    for class_name in lc_factory.class_names:
        if domain != "" and class_name.startswith(domain):
            class_name = class_name.removeprefix(f"{domain}_")
        try:
            lc = lc_factory.create(class_name, domain=domain)
            all_load_case_names.append(lc.name)
        except ImportError:
            continue

    if model_name != "PreRunPostModel" and issubclass(model_class, PreRunPostModel):
        all_component_names = ComponentFactory().class_names
        matching_load_case_names = []
        for c in all_component_names:
            candidate_load_case_name = c.removeprefix(model_class.PRE_PROC_FAMILY + "_")
            if (
                c.startswith(model_class.PRE_PROC_FAMILY)
                and candidate_load_case_name in all_load_case_names
            ):
                matching_load_case_names.append(candidate_load_case_name)
    else:
        # TODO: for non PreRunPostModel, define the load cases used by a model explicitely (as class attribute).
        load_case_names = list(set(all_load_case_names))
        matching_load_case_names = []
        for load_case_name in load_case_names:
            if load_case_name == DUMMY_LOAD_CASE_NAME:
                continue
            try:
                create_model(
                    model_name,
                    load_case_name,
                    archive_manager="DirectoryArchive",
                )
                matching_load_case_names.append(load_case_name)
            except (ImportError, AttributeError):
                continue

    return sorted(matching_load_case_names)

Materials are discovered across |v|'s own material_lib and that of every installed plugin. A material is compatible with a model when it declares the same grammar_name as the model's material grammar; the model's own material always comes first.

Parameters:

def get_available_materials(model_name: str = "") -> list[MaterialInfo]:
    """Find the materials a model can be built with.

    Materials are discovered across |v|'s own ``material_lib`` and that of every
    installed plugin. A material is compatible with a model when it declares the same
    ``grammar_name`` as the model's material grammar; the model's own material always
    comes first.

    Args:
        model_name: The model name. By default, every discoverable material is returned,
            regardless of any model.

    Returns:
        The compatible materials, empty if the model declares no material at all.
    """
    from vimseo.material.material_registry import available_materials
    from vimseo.material.material_registry import compatible_materials

    if not model_name:
        return available_materials()
    return compatible_materials(model_name)

def get_available_models(load_case: str = "") -> list[str]:
    """Returns the list of the available models.

    Args:
        load_case: The considered load case. If specified, only the models
            using this load case are returned.

    Returns:
        The list of names of the available models.
    """
    from vimseo.core.model_factory import ModelFactory

    mf = ModelFactory()
    model_names = mf.class_names
    if load_case == "":
        model_names.remove("PreRunPostModel")
        model_names.remove("ModelComposition")
        return model_names
    model_to_lc = {}
    for model_name in model_names:
        model_to_lc[model_name] = get_available_load_cases(model_name)
    model_names = []
    for model, load_cases in model_to_lc.items():
        if load_case in load_cases:
            model_names.append(model)

    return sorted(model_names)

def load_model_results(
    references,
    archive_manager: str = "",
    directory_archive_root: str | Path = "",
    study_name: str = "",
):
    """Load model results from their references, without executing their models.

    A reference is a ``run_id``, ``run:{run_id}``, the job directory of a simulation
    or ``runs:/{mlflow_run_id}`` (see :mod:`vimseo.storage_management.tool_archive.uri`),
    e.g. the ``uri`` of a summary of :func:`search_model_results` or the
    ``simulation_run_ids`` of a tool result. The class of a model must be installed.
    Its counterpart for the tool results is :func:`load_tool_results`.

    Args:
        references: One reference or a sequence of references.
        archive_manager: The archive manager of the simulations. If empty, guess it
            from the archive, else the one of the configuration.
        directory_archive_root: The root directory of the archive. If empty, the one
            of the configuration.
        study_name: Accepted so that the same archive settings are passed to every
            function; the results are searched in every study, whatever its value.

    Returns:
        The model results, a :class:`.ModelResults` in the order of the references,
        even for a single reference: ``load_model_results(ref)[0]``.

    Raises:
        KeyError: If a simulation is not in the archive.
    """
    from pandas import DataFrame

    from vimseo.core.model_result import ModelResult
    from vimseo.results.collection import ModelResults
    from vimseo.storage_management.base_archive_storage import create_simulation_summary
    from vimseo.storage_management.tool_archive.uri import load_model_data

    models = {}
    results = {}
    summaries = []
    for reference in _as_references(references):
        data = load_model_data(
            reference,
            archive_manager=archive_manager,
            directory_archive_root=directory_archive_root,
        )
        result = _from_model_data(ModelResult, data, models)
        summary = create_simulation_summary(
            result.to_dict(), result.study_name, f"run:{result.run_id}"
        )
        results[summary["run_id"]] = result
        summaries.append(summary)
    return ModelResults(
        DataFrame(summaries, columns=None if summaries else ["run_id", "status"]),
        lambda summary: results[summary["run_id"]],
        cache=dict(results),
    )

def load_tool_results(
    references,
    archive_manager: str = "",
    directory_archive_root: str | Path = "",
    study_name: str = "",
):
    """Load tool results from their references, without their tools.

    A reference is a ``tool_run_id``, ``tool-run:{tool_run_id}``, a result file, the
    directory of a tool run or ``runs:/{mlflow_run_id}`` (see
    :mod:`vimseo.storage_management.tool_archive.uri`), e.g. the ``uri`` of a summary
    of :func:`search_tool_runs`. Its counterpart for the model results is
    :func:`load_model_results`.

    Args:
        references: One reference or a sequence of references.
        archive_manager: The archive manager of the tool results, used by the
            identifiers. If empty, guess it from the archive.
        directory_archive_root: The root directory of the archive. If empty, the one
            of the configuration.
        study_name: Accepted so that the same archive settings are passed to every
            function; the results are searched in every study, whatever its value.

    Returns:
        The tool results, a :class:`.ToolResults` in the order of the references,
        even for a single reference: ``load_tool_results(ref)[0]``.
    """
    from pandas import DataFrame

    from vimseo.results.collection import ToolResults
    from vimseo.results.collection import create_tool_summary
    from vimseo.storage_management.tool_archive.base_tool_archive import create_summary
    from vimseo.storage_management.tool_archive.uri import load_tool_result

    results = {}
    summaries = []
    for reference in _as_references(references):
        result = load_tool_result(
            reference,
            archive_manager=archive_manager,
            directory_archive_root=directory_archive_root,
        )
        metadata = result.metadata
        summary = create_tool_summary({
            **create_summary(
                "",
                metadata.tool_run_id,
                metadata.parent_tool_run_id,
                "FINISHED",
                result=result,
            ),
            "tool_name": metadata.misc.get("tool_name", type(result).__name__),
            "uri": str(reference),
        })
        results[summary["tool_run_id"]] = result
        summaries.append(summary)
    return ToolResults(
        DataFrame(summaries, columns=None if summaries else ["tool_run_id", "status"]),
        lambda summary: results[summary["tool_run_id"]],
        cache=dict(results),
    )

def open_tool_results(
    archive_manager: str = "",
    directory_archive_root: str | Path = "",
    study_name: str = "",
    query: str = "",
    failed: bool | None = None,
    **metadata,
):
    """Open the tool results of an archive, as a collection.

    Args:
        archive_manager: The archive manager of the tool results. If empty, the one of
            the configuration.
        directory_archive_root: The root directory of the archive. If empty, the one
            of the configuration.
        study_name: The study. If empty, every study.
        query: A query on the summaries, see :mod:`vimseo.results.query`.
        failed: Whether to keep only the failed tool runs (``True``), only the others
            (``False``) or both (``None``).
        **metadata: Values of metadata, e.g. ``tool_name="DOETool"``.

    Returns:
        The tool results, a :class:`.ToolResults`.
    """
    from pandas import DataFrame

    from vimseo.results.collection import ToolResults
    from vimseo.results.collection import create_tool_summary
    from vimseo.storage_management.tool_archive.uri import load_tool_result

    summaries = [
        create_tool_summary(summary)
        for summary in search_tool_runs(
            archive_manager, directory_archive_root, study_name
        )
    ]

    def load(summary):
        return load_tool_result(
            summary["uri"],
            archive_manager=archive_manager,
            directory_archive_root=directory_archive_root,
        )

    return ToolResults(
        DataFrame(summaries, columns=None if summaries else ["tool_run_id", "status"]),
        load,
    ).filter(query, failed, **metadata)

def search_model_results(
    archive_manager: str = "",
    directory_archive_root: str | Path = "",
    study_name: str = "",
    model_name: str = "",
    load_case: str = "",
    status: str = "FINISHED",
    query: str = "",
) -> list[dict]:
    """Search the archived simulations, without loading their results.

    Its counterpart for the tool runs is :func:`search_tool_runs`.

    Args:
        archive_manager: The archive manager of the simulations, ``"DirectoryArchive"``
            or ``"MlflowArchive"``. If empty, the one of the configuration.
        directory_archive_root: The root directory of the archive. If empty, the one
            of the configuration.
        study_name: The study. If empty, every study.
        model_name: The name of the model. If empty, every model.
        load_case: The name of the load case. If empty, every load case.
        status: The status of the simulations. If empty, every status.
        query: A query on the summaries, e.g.
            ``"`inputs.height` > 45 or load_case == 'ThreePoints'"``, see
            :mod:`vimseo.results.query`.

    Returns:
        One summary per simulation, from the oldest to the newest: ``run_id``,
        ``study_name``, ``model_name``, ``load_case``, ``status``, ``datetime``,
        ``tool_run_id``, ``uri`` (to load it with :func:`load_model_results`), some
        metadata, and the scalar inputs and outputs as ``inputs.{name}`` and
        ``outputs.{name}``.
    """
    from pandas import DataFrame

    from vimseo.results.query import apply_query
    from vimseo.results.query import to_mlflow_filter

    archive_manager, directory_archive_root = _resolve_archive(
        archive_manager, directory_archive_root
    )
    archive = _open_simulation_archive(archive_manager, directory_archive_root)
    options = {}
    if archive_manager == "MlflowArchive":
        # The conjunctive part of the query is evaluated by the server too.
        names = _get_mlflow_names([])
        names.update({
            name: f"metrics.`{name}`" for name in _get_query_names(query, "inputs.")
        })
        names.update({
            name: f"metrics.`{name[len('outputs.') :]}`"
            for name in _get_query_names(query, "outputs.")
        })
        options["filter_string"] = to_mlflow_filter(query, names)
    summaries = archive.search_results(
        model_name=model_name,
        load_case=load_case,
        study_name=study_name,
        status=status,
        **options,
    )
    if not query:
        return summaries
    return apply_query(DataFrame(summaries), query).to_dict("records")

def search_tool_runs(
    archive_manager: str = "",
    directory_archive_root: str | Path = "",
    study_name: str = "",
    tool_name: str = "",
    status: str = "",
    query: str = "",
) -> list[dict]:
    """Search the archived tool runs, without loading their results.

    Its counterpart for the simulations is :func:`search_model_results`.

    Args:
        archive_manager: The archive manager of the tool results. If empty, the one of
            the configuration.
        directory_archive_root: The root directory of the archive. If empty, the one
            of the configuration.
        study_name: The study. If empty, every study.
        tool_name: The name of the tool. If empty, every tool.
        status: The status of the tool runs. If empty, every status.
        query: A query on the summaries, see :mod:`vimseo.results.query`; the
            settings are ``inputs.{name}`` and the key values ``outputs.{name}``.

    Returns:
        One summary per tool run, from the oldest to the newest, with its ``uri``
        (to load it with :func:`load_tool_results`).
    """
    from pandas import DataFrame

    from vimseo.results.collection import create_tool_summary
    from vimseo.results.query import apply_query
    from vimseo.storage_management.tool_archive.uri import get_default_archive_manager

    tool_archive_manager = open_tool_archive(
        archive_manager or get_default_archive_manager(), directory_archive_root
    )
    summaries = sorted(
        tool_archive_manager.search_tool_runs(
            tool_name=tool_name, status=status, study_name=study_name
        ),
        key=operator.itemgetter("tool_run_id"),
    )
    if not query:
        return summaries
    flat = DataFrame([create_tool_summary(summary) for summary in summaries])
    kept = set(apply_query(flat, query)["tool_run_id"]) if not flat.empty else set()
    return [summary for summary in summaries if summary["tool_run_id"] in kept]

docs.title: star_doe
docs.text:
The DOE used by a star One-factor-at-a-Time (OAT) sensitivity analysis.

From a center :math:x_0, the star DOE varies each component :math:i of the variables by a physical step :math:h_i while the other components remain at the center:

.. math::

x_0,\ x_0+h_1e_1,\ \ldots,\ x_0+h_de_d \quad\left[,\ x_0-h_1e_1,\ \ldots,\ x_0-h_de_d\right]

where the points in brackets are added when the DOE is two-sided.

Contrary to the GEMSEO OATDOE, whose points form a trajectory (the steps accumulate from a point to the next one) and whose step is defined in the unit hypercube (i.e. in probability for a random variable), all the effects are measured around the same center and the step is defined in the physical space, whatever the probability distribution of the variable.

BaseDisciplineModel(
    load_case_name: str = "Dummy", **options

Bases: IntegratedModel

A model wrapping a single GEMSEO :class:~gemseo.core.discipline.Discipline.

The wrapped discipline is provided through the _DISCIPLINE class attribute.

Notes

Since an IntegratedModel extends a GEMSEO <https://gemseo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/index.html>_ :class:~.gemseo.core.discipline.MDODiscipline, it can be used as |gemseo| discipline <https://gemseo.readthedocs.io/en/6.0.0/examples/api /plot_discipline.html#discipline>_. Also, |gemseo| capabilities (MLearning, Optimisation) can be used on the model.

Examples:

>>> # Run a model with default values, each execution being stored in a unique
>>> # directory. The archive and scratch persistency is customized.
>>> # The manager for archiving the results is set to MLFlow.
>>> from vimseo.api import create_model
>>> from vimseo.core.model_settings import IntegratedModelSettings
>>> model = create_model("BendingTestAnalytical", "Cantilever",
>>>     model_options=IntegratedModelSettings(
>>>         directory_archive_root=f"my_model_result",
>>>         directory_scratch_root=f"my_scratch",
>>>         directory_scratch_persistency=PersistencyPolicy.DELETE_ALWAYS,
>>>         directory_archive_persistency=PersistencyPolicy.DELETE_IF_FAULTY,
>>>         archive_manager="MlflowArchive",
>>>     ),
>>> )
>>> model.execute()

Initialize self. See help(type(self)) for accurate signature.

def __init__(self, load_case_name: str = "Dummy", **options):
    options = IntegratedModelSettings(**options).model_dump()
    if load_case_name != self._EXPECTED_LOAD_CASE:
        msg = f"The load case should be {self._EXPECTED_LOAD_CASE}."
        raise ImportError(msg)
    super().__init__(
        load_case_name,
        [DisciplineWrapperComponent(load_case_name, deepcopy(self._DISCIPLINE))],
        **options,
    )

docs.title: PLOTS class-attribute
docs.text:
PLOTS: Sequence[Plot | tuple[str, ...]] = []

The figures to plot from the model data.

A figure is defined either by a tuple of variable names, the first one being the abscissa and the following ones the ordinates, or by a :class:.Plot when the lines shall be styled, drawn against a secondary ordinate axis or completed with horizontal reference lines.

A load case can override or extend these figures by declaring its own PLOTS class attribute. A load-case entry whose abscissa and first ordinate match a model entry replaces it in place; any other entry is appended. See :class:.LoadCase and :func:.merge_plots.

Examples:

>>> # A single line, and two lines sharing an abscissa.
>>> PLOTS = [
...     ("strain_history", "stress_history"),
...     ("time", "energy_strain_history", "energy_damage_history"),
... ]

>>> # A styled figure with a secondary ordinate axis and a custom abscissa
>>> # label.
>>> PLOTS = [
...     Plot(
...         x="displacement_history",
...         x_label="Displacement",
...         traces=[
...             Trace("force_history", style=LineStyle(color="blue")),
...             Trace(
...                 "crack_position_history",
...                 secondary_y=True,
...                 style=LineStyle(color="red", marker="."),
...             ),
...         ],
...         title="Crack propagation",
...     )
... ]

docs.text:
archive_outputs(output_data)

Archive the model result: field files, metadata, results, persistent files.

Runs the archive half of the execute tail against the current scratch job directory — collecting field files (:meth:_collect_field_files), generating the metadata into output_data, then writing results.json and copying the persistent files through the archive manager. The archive job directory must already be created (self._archive_manager.create_job_directory()). Unlike :meth:_manage_persistency it does not touch the scratch-persistency policy, so a caller that ran individual disciplines (the vtt GUI's pre/run/post flow) can archive exactly as model.execute does without deleting the job directory it is reading.

Source code in src\vimseo\core\base_integrated_model.py 
def archive_outputs(self, output_data):
    """Archive the model result: field files, metadata, results, persistent files.

    Runs the archive half of the ``execute`` tail against the current scratch
    job directory — collecting field files (:meth:`_collect_field_files`),
    generating the metadata into *output_data*, then writing ``results.json``
    and copying the persistent files through the archive manager. The archive
    job directory must already be created
    (``self._archive_manager.create_job_directory()``). Unlike
    :meth:`_manage_persistency` it does **not** touch the scratch-persistency
    policy, so a caller that ran individual disciplines (the vtt GUI's
    pre/run/post flow) can archive exactly as ``model.execute`` does without
    deleting the job directory it is reading.
    """
    self._collect_field_files(output_data)

    meta_data = self.generate_metadata(output_data)
    output_data.update(asdict(meta_data))

    result_model = {"inputs": self.get_input_data(), "outputs": output_data}
    self._archive_manager.enforce_persistency_policy(result_model)
    self._archive_manager.copy_persistent_files(self._scratch_manager.job_directory)
    return output_data

def auto_get_file(
    self,
    file_suffix: str,
    load_cases: Iterable[str] = (),
) -> Iterable[Path]:
    """Return file paths for files following a naming convention and placed next to
    the model class or its parents, or next to a model load case class. Naming
    convention is {model_class_name}{file_suffix} or
    {model_class_name}_{load_case}{file_suffix}.

    Args:
        file_suffix: The suffix, including the extension, of the file to be searched
            in next to model class or its parents.
        load_cases: an iterable of load cases. If specified, only the files placed
            next to these load case classes are searched.
            Otherwise, all load case classes associated to the model are considered.

    Returns:
        A list of file paths.
    """
    from vimseo.api import get_available_load_cases

    cls = self.__class__
    model_name = cls.__name__
    load_cases = load_cases or get_available_load_cases(model_name)
    classes = [cls] + [
        base for base in cls.__bases__ if issubclass(base, Discipline)
    ]
    names = [model_name] + [cls.__name__ for cls in classes[1:]]

    matching_files = []
    for cls, name in zip(classes, names, strict=False):
        class_module = sys.modules[cls.__module__]
        directory_path = Path(class_module.__file__).parent.absolute()
        file_path = directory_path / f"{name}{file_suffix}"
        if file_path.is_file():
            matching_files.append(file_path)
        for load_case in load_cases:
            file_path = directory_path / f"{name}_{load_case}{file_suffix}"
            if file_path.is_file():
                matching_files.append(file_path)

    if not matching_files:
        msg = (
            f"No files with suffix {file_suffix} were found next "
            f"to the model {self.name} or its parent class."
        )
        raise FileNotFoundError(msg)

    return matching_files

def create_cache_from_archive(
    self, run_ids: Iterable[str] | None = None
) -> HDF5Cache:
    """Defines a temporary HDF5 cache file, based on results found on the current
    archive.

    Args:
        run_ids: The IDs of the runs to put in the cache.
            If ``None``, use all the runs of the current archive or experiment.
            If empty, the cache is empty.
    """

    # cache file preparation
    cache_dir_path = Path(self._cache_file_path).parent
    self._cache_file_path = Path(
        cache_dir_path
        / f"{self.__class__.__name__}_{self._load_case.name}_from_archive.hdf"
    )
    self._cache_file_path.unlink(
        missing_ok=True
    )  # delete possible old tmp cache file
    # note that tolerance is important for now: see issue #233.

    self.set_cache(
        cache_type=Discipline.CacheType.HDF5,
        hdf_file_path=self._cache_file_path,
        hdf_node_path="node",
        tolerance=1.0e-10,
    )

    results = self._archive_manager.get_archived_results(run_ids=run_ids)
    if results is None:
        return None

    for result in results:
        if not isinstance(self.cache, SimpleCache):
            to_array = self.output_grammar.data_converter.convert_value_to_array
            for name, value in result["outputs"].items():
                result["outputs"][name] = to_array(name, value)

        self.cache.cache_outputs(result["inputs"], result["outputs"])
        # jacobian = None
        #
        # # append a cache entry with the current result
        # self.cache[result["inputs"]] = (result["outputs"], jacobian)

    return self.cache

def get_dataflow(self):
    """The inputs and outputs of the components of the model.

    Returns:
         A dictionary mapping component name to its input and output names.
    """

    dataflow = {
        "model_inputs": self.get_input_data_names(),
        "model_outputs": self.get_output_data_names(),
    }

    for component in self._chain.disciplines:
        dataflow[component.name] = {
            "inputs": list(component.input_grammar.names),
            "outputs": list(component.output_grammar.names),
        }

    return dataflow

def get_output_data_names(self, remove_metadata: bool = False) -> list[str]:
    """

    Args:
        remove_metadata: Whether to remove the metadata from the output data names.

    """
    output_data_names = list(self.output_grammar.names)

    if remove_metadata:
        for name in self.get_metadata_names():
            if name in output_data_names:
                output_data_names.remove(name)

    return output_data_names

def plot_results(
    self,
    directory_path: str | Path = "",
    save: bool = True,
    show: bool = False,
    scalar_names: Iterable[str] = (),
    data: str = "PLOTS",
) -> Mapping[str, Figure]:
    """Plots the results, from the definition of the figures in the PLOTS variable.

    Args:
        directory_path: A path where to save the plots, in files prefixed by the
            names of the model and of the load case. If empty, the job directory
            of the simulation in the archive, where the files are not prefixed
            (the path already names the model and the load case), else the
            current working directory.
        save: Whether to save the plot.
        show: Whether to show the plot.
        scalar_names: The scalars to plot in a scatter matrix. Show all scalars by default.
        data: Either ``"PLOTS"`` to draw the figures defined in ``PLOTS``,
            or ``"SCALARS"`` to draw a scatter matrix of the scalar outputs.

    Returns:
        The figures, indexed by their name.
    """
    # The job directory already names the model and the load case: a prefix
    # would only lengthen paths, which are limited to 260 characters on Windows.
    prefix = (
        f"{self.name}_{self._load_case.name}_"
        if directory_path != "" or not self.archive_manager.job_directory
        else ""
    )
    if save:
        directory_path = (
            Path(directory_path)
            if directory_path != ""
            else Path(self.archive_manager.job_directory or Path.cwd())
        )
        if not directory_path.exists():
            directory_path.mkdir(parents=True)
        LOGGER.info(f"Saving plots to {directory_path.absolute()}")
    else:
        directory_path = ""

    from vimseo.core.model_result import ModelResult

    result = ModelResult.from_dict(
        {"inputs": self.get_input_data(), "outputs": self.get_output_data()},
        model=self,
    )
    figures = {}
    if data == "PLOTS":
        figures = self._plot_curves(
            figures, result, directory_path, save, show, prefix
        )
    elif data == "SCALARS":
        plot = ScatterMatrix(
            Dataset.from_dataframe(
                DataFrame.from_dict([result.scalars(variable_names=scalar_names)])
            )
        )
        figures["scalars"] = plot.execute(
            directory_path=directory_path,
            file_name="scalars.html",
            save=save,
            show=show,
        )
    else:
        msg = f"Unknown data type {data} for plotting."
        raise ValueError(msg)

    return figures
